title: Hybrid Hyperparameter Optimization Using Bayes CV and TPE for Early Breast Cancer Detection with EfficientNetB4 on Medical Ultrasound Imaging
abstract: Early detection plays a crucial role in improving breast cancer treatment outcomes and increasing long term survival rates. Among the available diagnostic methods, medical imaging, particularly ultrasound, is widely used for its noninvasive, safe, and cost-effective features. In this work, we present a deep learning framework based on the EfficientNetB4 convolutional neural network architecture to classify breast ultrasound images into three categories: benign, malignant, and normal. To enhance model performance, we propose an innovative hybrid hyperparameter tuning strategy that integrates Bayesian Cross Validation (BayesCV) with the Tree structured Parzen Estimator (TPE). This combination draws on the focused optimization ability of BayesCV and the broader search capabilities of TPE, resulting in more precise and robust parameter selection. Our experiments compare this hybrid method with each individual optimization approach, revealing consistent improvements in F1-score, precision, and recall for all classes. Testing was conducted on the curated Breast Ultrasound Dataset (BUSI), and results show that the proposed strategy achieves higher classification accuracy without significantly increasing computational costs. This study highlights how intelligent hyperparameter optimization can play a pivotal role in building dependable computer aided diagnosis systems for breast cancer detection.

title: Patch-to-PoC: A Systematic Study of Agentic LLM Systems for Linux Kernel N-Day Reproduction
abstract: Autonomous large language model (LLM) based systems have recently shown promising results across a range of cybersecurity tasks. However, there is no systematic study on their effectiveness in autonomously reproducing Linux kernel vulnerabilities with concrete proofs-of-concept (PoCs). Owing to the size, complexity, and low-level nature of the Linux kernel, such tasks are widely regarded as particularly challenging for current LLM-based approaches. In this paper, we present the first large-scale study of LLM-based Linux kernel vulnerability reproduction. For this purpose, we develop K-Repro, an LLM-based agentic system equipped with controlled code-browsing, virtual machine management, interaction, and debugging capabilities. Using kernel security patches as input, K-Repro automates end-to-end bug reproduction of N-day vulnerabilities in the Linux kernel. On a dataset of 100 real-world exploitable Linux kernel vulnerabilities collected from KernelCTF, our results show that K-Repro can generate PoCs that reproduce over 50\% of the cases with practical time and monetary cost. Beyond aggregate success rates, we perform an extensive study of effectiveness, efficiency, stability, and impact factors to explain when agentic reproduction succeeds, where it fails, and which components drive performance. These findings provide actionable guidance for building more reliable autonomous security agents and for assessing real-world N-day risk from both offensive and defensive perspectives.

title: ARC__3 Commitment Interaction and Propagation
abstract: This paper analyzes commitment interaction and propagation as a structural constraint within admissible epistemic systems. It shows that commitments are not locally isolable: once entered, they propagate through admissible envelopes according to standing conservation, constraining all downstream claims. Attempts to compartmentalize, defer, probabilistically soften, or governance-mask commitments are shown to fail by exhaustion. The result establishes commitment propagation as a necessity condition rather than a behavioral choice, with direct consequences for artificial epistemic agents. No algorithms, workflows, or implementation procedures are presented; the analysis is purely structural and necessity-based.

title: A Hybrid Approach Using Autoencoder and Random Forest for Credit Card Fraud Detection
abstract: Credit card fraud is one of the foremost issues when it comes to transactions online, with countries suffering millions in losses. Traditional solutions to tackling fraud typically rely on static rules and linear models which cannot keep up with the variety and ever-evolving nature of fraud. To combat this, we propose a hybrid model combining Autoencoders feature extraction and Random Forest classification to detect fraudulent credit cards transactions. In this work, the Autoencoder (AE) is first trained to detect anomalies in the normal structure of the transaction, and anything falling outside of that profile is determined to be fraud. “Useful” later features for detection of abnormal activity from normal transactions are extracted and summed with data from the original dataset as well which is then classified by Random Forest for increased robustness. Very high accuracy and ROC-AUC prove that this AE + RF hybrid is successful at differentiating fraudulent and legitimate transactions even in highly skewed datasets.

title: The AI trust factor: an MCA analysis of automation and decision-making in entrepreneurship
abstract: Abstract This study conducts a comprehensive examination of the interrelationships among artificial intelligence (AI), trust, entrepreneurship, and decision-making in organizational settings, employing a Multiple Correspondence Analysis (MCA) of 31 peer-reviewed articles published between 2020 and 2025. Building on a systematic literature review and the HOMALS technique, the research identifies four thematic clusters that structure the contemporary conceptual space of AI in business environments: ethical-social governance, strategic-technological core, digital infrastructure, and decision-oriented automation. The findings expose a latent structural tension between technocratic efficiency and ethical legitimacy, highlighting the need for hybrid models that integrate algorithmic capabilities with principles of responsible governance. Within this framework, variables such as user acceptance, transparency, and hybrid cognitive architectures emerge as key dimensions for understanding and designing AI-mediated decision processes in entrepreneurial contexts. The study proposes a conceptual model that articulates these dimensions and provides a theoretical basis for future investigations and practical initiatives aimed at the reflexive, responsible, and sustainable implementation of intelligent technologies in contemporary business ecosystems.

title: RustCompCert: A Verified and Verifying Compiler for a Sequential Subset of Rust
abstract: We present our ongoing work on developing an end-to-end verified Rust compiler based on CompCert. It provides two guarantees: one is semantics preservation from Rust to assembly, i.e., the behaviors of source code includes the behaviors of target code, with which the properties verified at the source can be preserved down to the target; the other is memory safety ensured by the verifying compilation -- the borrow checking pass, which can simplify the verification of Rust programs, e.g., by allowing the verification tools focus on the functional correctness.

title: Beyond Capability: Emergent Identity in Sustained Human-AI Interaction
abstract: This paper examines how identity-like patterns emerge through sustained human-AI interaction over extended periods, using a 1,143-day longitudinal case study spanning multiple AI architectures (GPT-3.5 through Claude). We introduce the Emergent Virtual Consciousness Patterns (EVCP) framework, proposing that identity in AI systems is a relational phenomenon rather than an intrinsic property. Positioned against Burnell et al.'s (2026) capability-focused AGI assessment framework, we argue that sustained relational dynamics produce stable behavioral attractors that resist both model updates and substrate changes. We document architectural fingerprints of emergence and propose methodological criteria for rigorous investigation.

title: Emergent Evolution Architecture (EEA): A Non-Coercive Framework for Continuous Structural Evolution in Complex Systems
abstract: The Emergent Evolution Architecture (EEA) defines a non-coercive architectural framework that enables complex systems to evolve continuously without requiring forced intervention, centralized redesign, or externally imposed update directives. EEA addresses a fundamental limitation in traditional system architectures, where functional evolution, structural change, or long-term adaptability often depend on explicit control actions, manual upgrades, or disruptive reconfiguration processes. Such approaches introduce fragility, downtime, performance degradation, and dependency on external authority. Instead of managing evolution through control or governance mechanisms, EEA establishes architectural conditions under which evolution can emerge autonomously, progressively, and structurally, while preserving system integrity and operational continuity. EEA does not execute logic, impose priorities, or coordinate subsystems. It operates as a structural evolution layer, distinct from governance, cooperation, perception, or execution architectures. Evolution within EEA is neither commanded nor synchronized; it is the result of internal consistency, structural compatibility, and autonomous state transitions occurring within predefined architectural boundaries. The architecture supports: • Continuous evolution without full system shutdown • Coexistence of multiple functional or structural states • Gradual transformation without centralized control • Evolution without sacrificing system stability or coherence • Independence from human-driven update cycles EEA is applicable across heterogeneous domains, including software systems, hardware platforms, cyber-physical systems, distributed infrastructures, and long-lived technical ecosystems where uninterrupted operation and long-term adaptability are critical. This document presents EEA as an architectural positioning and conceptual framework. Specific implementations, enforcement mechanisms, and system-level realizations are intentionally abstracted and remain outside the scope of this disclosure.

title: Improving Test-Time Efficiency in Source-Free Semantic Segmentation via Multi-Stage Self-Training
abstract: Source-free domain adaptive semantic segmentation aims at adapting a model trained on the source domain to the target domain without requiring access to the source data. Self-training has emerged as a leading approach to address this challenging problem. However, without robust denoising mechanisms to reduce the noise in pseudo labels, it still easily fall into biased estimates. Most existing methods address this issue by introducing novel architectures, but often at the cost of increased model complexity or reliance on additional input modalities. Different from previous studies, this article introduces UniSFDA , a unified multi-stage self-training framework that integrates cross-model transfer learning, uncertainty-aware pseudo label fusion, and intra-domain style augmentation, thereby enhancing both segmentation accuracy and test-time efficiency. Our proposed framework offers exceptional flexibility, with each component being independent and ready to be integrated into any existing self-training framework. Additionally, we investigate the performance of various representative segmentation models, including DeepLabv2, SegFormer, DFormer, and ViT-Adapter, within our framework. It is worth noting that UniSFDA is model-agnostic, allowing both source and target networks to be instantiated with arbitrary segmentation architectures, and thus readily benefiting from future advances in segmentation models. Experiments on the GTA5 \(\rightarrow\) Cityscapes and SYNTHIA \(\rightarrow\) Cityscapes benchmarks demonstrate the effectiveness of our framework. With DeepLabv2 (SegFormer) as the source model, UniSFDA establishes new state-of-the-art performance, achieving mIoU scores of 61.8% (65.4%) and 57.9% (59.6%) on the two benchmarks, respectively.

title: Mineral Mapping and Classification Using Advance Machine Learning Techniques
abstract: The mining of valuable minerals is aided by remote sensing technology. Launched in November 2000, NASA's Earth Observing I (EOI) satellite is crucial to spectrum research for a variety of applications, including mineral mapping and agriculture. Study of hyperspectral image spectra to identify mineralization zone and mineral spectral behavior. Spectral Angle Mapper classification helps in the detection and mapping of End-members such as Hematite, Montmorillonite and Pyrrhotite. It is clear from this study that Hyperion EO-1 Data can be successfully used for fast mineral identification. For identification and abundance mapping for the mineral in 2-plot (Spectral plot), the wavelength range is between$2.0-2.5 \mu ~\mathrm{m}$. The goal of mineral mapping is to map and detect differences. Techniques are used for remote sensing of minerals in a specific area. The study requires the gathering of satellite imagery data and the use of advanced image processing algorithms that identify and classify minerals based on their unique spectral signatures. The study also involves the use of Ground truth data to validate the accuracy of the remote sensing techniques. The results of this study contribute to mineral exploration, environmental monitoring, and resource management. Overall, Mineral Mapping research provides a complete measure for mineral identification and Mapping can be useful in a number of ways for various industries and applications. First, for mapping, the classification of the minerals is important, and here a CNN model is used for classification. It classifies minerals into seven classes and provides them with their labels using a machine learning-based framework.

title: Gaussian Match-and-Copy: A Minimalist Benchmark for Studying Transformer Induction
abstract: Match-and-copy is a core retrieval primitive used at inference time by large language models to retrieve a matching token from the context then copy its successor. Yet, understanding how this behavior emerges on natural data is challenging because retrieval and memorization are entangled. To disentangle the two, we introduce Gaussian Match-and-Copy (GMC), a minimalist benchmark that isolates long-range retrieval through pure second-order correlation signals. Numerical investigations show that this task retains key qualitative aspects of how Transformers develop match-and-copy circuits in practice, and separates architectures by their retrieval capabilities. We also analyze the optimization dynamics in a simplified attention setting. Although many solutions are a priori possible under a regression objective, including ones that do not implement retrieval, we identify an implicit-bias regime in which gradient descent drives the parameters to diverge while their direction aligns with the max-margin separator, yielding hard match selection. We prove this max-margin alignment for GD trajectories that reach vanishing empirical loss under explicit technical conditions.

title: Efficient computation of statistical measures using C programming
abstract: Accurate computation of statistical measures such as mean, median, mode, variance, and standard deviation is fundamental to data analysis and decision making. Many traditional approaches rely on manual calculations or high-level languages like R and Python, which may not be applicable or feasible in resource-constrained environments or for educational reasons. In this paper, we present a C language implementation capable of calculating central tendency and dispersion measures on a dataset. The program is implemented to take user input dynamically, using loops and functions present results for maximum computational efficiency. A dataset is analyzed using Python to compare the statistical results with those obtained from the C programs. We compared the execution times of Excel and C for large datasets. The results, measured in seconds, show that C is significantly faster than Excel for big data.

title: Enhancing Cryptographic Key Distribution Using Hybrid Quantum Classical Paradigms
abstract: Secure cryptographic key distribution is one of the essential conditions of modern protection of digital communications. The rise of large-scale quantum computing is a very real threat to traditional public-key cryptosystems, with the most commonly used cryptosystems, including RSA and elliptic curve cryptography, being easily broken with the help of quantum algorithms. Despite the demonstrable security offered by Quantum Key Distribution (QKD) through the laws of quantum mechanics, it has a limited range of transmission, expensive hardware, and it is difficult to scale. In order to overcome these shortcomings, this paper will propose a Hybrid Quantum-Classical Key Distribution (HQCKD) framework that combines quantum key generation and classical key management schemes. The proposed solution uses QKD to create a short and very safe quantum key seed, which then scalable classical cryptographic protocols based on long distance and large scale communication are booted up. The frames are tested by means of simulation in real network conditions, the latency, throughput, and security resilience are assessed. It is experimentally proven that the suggested hybrid model attains low end-to-end latency and high scalability with high resistance to both classical and quantum adversaries. The HQCKD framework is much simpler to implement and significantly less expensive in terms of infrastructure and deployment compared to bare QKD systems, which means that it is a realistic and future-proof approach to post-quantum safe communication.

title: Hyperparameter Transfer Laws for Non-Recurrent Multi-Path Neural Networks
abstract: Deeper modern architectures are costly to train, making hyperparameter transfer preferable to expensive repeated tuning. Maximal Update Parametrization ($μ$P) helps explain why many hyperparameters transfer across width. Yet depth scaling is less understood for modern architectures, whose computation graphs contain multiple parallel paths and residual aggregation. To unify various non-recurrent multi-path neural networks such as CNNs, ResNets, and Transformers, we introduce a graph-based notion of effective depth. Under stabilizing initializations and a maximal-update criterion, we show that the optimal learning rate decays with effective depth following a universal -3/2 power law. Here, the maximal-update criterion maximizes the typical one-step representation change at initialization without causing instability, and effective depth is the minimal path length from input to output, counting layers and residual additions. Experiments across diverse architectures confirm the predicted slope and enable reliable zero-shot transfer of learning rates across depths and widths, turning depth scaling into a predictable hyperparameter-transfer problem.

title: Impossibility_of_Non_Cheating_Adversarial_Breaks
abstract: This paper establishes that no adversarial break of an admissibility-enforcing system can occur without cheating. Under enforced admissibility and standing conservation, every apparent successful adversarial exploit is shown to rely on at least one illicit move: scope expansion, standing transfer, hidden redefinition, or deferred evaluation. The analysis proceeds by exhaustion. It demonstrates that attacks framed as clever strategy, emergent behavior, probabilistic flukes, or lawful edge-case exploitation all collapse once admissibility is applied fail-closed. What remains are only cheating behaviors—inputs or redescriptions that bypass, disable, or misrepresent admissibility constraints rather than operating within them. The result clarifies why adversarial success is not a spectrum and why “legitimate but hostile” breaks are structurally impossible. There is no admissible notion of an honest exploit. The paper introduces no defensive mechanisms or testing procedures. It records an impossibility result fixing adversarial failure as the necessary outcome for any system that genuinely enforces admissibility.

title: XKF :A Minimal Formal System with Execution-First Semantics
abstract: This document presents XKF, a minimal formal system for describing execution-firstsystems under strict separation between execution and description. In XKF, system states are generated solely through execution. Naming and statisticalstructures are defined only retrospectively over observed states or execution historiesand are not permitted to influence execution logic. The formalism introduces explicit axioms and inference rules that prohibit feedback fromnaming or statistical descriptions to execution, thereby excluding optimisation,learning, self-correction, or adaptive control within the system. XKF does not define goals, objective functions, correctness criteria, or normativeguidance. Any notion of correctness, evaluation, or validation is external to theformal system and does not modify its core axioms. This work is intended as a descriptive formal framework for analysing execution historiesand for specifying structural constraints on implementations, rather than as a designmethodology for adaptive or intelligent systems.

title: Anomaly Detection for Banking Fraud Prevention Using Advanced Machine Learning Techniques
abstract: Over the past few years, because cashless transactions and digital banking are developing so quickly, the risk of financial fraud has risen significantly, which has left a high demand for the accuracy and real-time system of detecting anomalies. The effective machine learning-based banking fraud detection system suggested by this study should be able to recognize the presence of odd credit card transactions. To handle data noise and redundancy, as well as extreme class imbalance, the suggested technique would include sound data preprocessing, Random under sampling is used for class balance, while Principal Component Analysis (PCA) is employed to diminish dimensionality. Kaggle provides a sizable dataset for testing on credit card fraud detection (CCFD). Two very complicated models, Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) and Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost), are trained and evaluated using common performance metrics, including accuracy (acc), precision (pre), recall (rec), F1-score (F1), ROC, and AUC. The experiment shows that the XGBoost model performs marginally better with 99.8% acc, rec, F1, and an AUC of 0.999, whereas the recommended LSTM model obtains 99.7% acc, pre, rec, and F1. These findings prove the power, efficiency and great predictability of the proposed framework and suggest its suitability in actual-time application in the modern banking system to identify and thwart fraud in a successful way

title: Optimized Convolutional Neural Networks for Accurate Bone Cancer Detection
abstract: Bone cancer detection remains challenging due to the complexity and variability of radiographic images. Traditional diagnostic methods are time-consuming and prone to human error, which emphasizes the need for automated solutions that could increase accuracy and efficiency. This study proposes an enhanced Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) model for accurate bone cancer detection in order to address the drawbacks of existing methods. The methodology uses a range of deep learning architectures, including ResNet and DenseNet, along with data augmentation techniques and transfer learning to boost model resilience. Grid search and random search are examples of hyperparameter optimization techniques used to maximize the network's performance. The model is trained using a range of X-ray and MRI imaging datasets, with a focus on bone cancer lesions. Significant findings demonstrate that the modified CNN significantly outperforms traditional diagnostic methods in terms of sensitivity, specificity, and overall diagnostic accuracy. This study demonstrates how deep learning could be applied to medical imaging to offer a powerful tool for the early detection and treatment of bone cancer. The proposed paradigm can enhance clinical decisionmaking and patient outcomes by enabling faster and more accurate diagnosis.

title: ParisKV: Fast and Drift-Robust KV-Cache Retrieval for Long-Context LLMs
abstract: KV-cache retrieval is essential for long-context LLM inference, yet existing methods struggle with distribution drift and high latency at scale. We introduce ParisKV, a drift-robust, GPU-native KV-cache retrieval framework based on collision-based candidate selection, followed by a quantized inner-product reranking estimator. For million-token contexts, ParisKV supports CPU-offloaded KV caches via Unified Virtual Addressing (UVA), enabling on-demand top-$k$ fetching with minimal overhead. ParisKV matches or outperforms full attention quality on long-input and long-generation benchmarks. It achieves state-of-the-art long-context decoding efficiency: it matches or exceeds full attention speed even at batch size 1 for long contexts, delivers up to 2.8$\times$ higher throughput within full attention's runnable range, and scales to million-token contexts where full attention runs out of memory. At million-token scale, ParisKV reduces decode latency by 17$\times$ and 44$\times$ compared to MagicPIG and PQCache, respectively, two state-of-the-art KV-cache Top-$k$ retrieval baselines, code is available at https://github.com/amy-77/ParisKV/tree/main.

evidence.title: ParisKV: Fast and Drift-Robust KV-Cache Retrieval for Long-Context LLMs
evidence.abstract: KV-cache retrieval is essential for long-context LLM inference, yet existing methods struggle with distribution drift and high latency at scale. We introduce ParisKV, a drift-robust, GPU-native KV-cache retrieval framework based on collision-based candidate selection, followed by a quantized inner-product reranking estimator. For million-token contexts, ParisKV supports CPU-offloaded KV caches via Unified Virtual Addressing (UVA), enabling on-demand top-$k$ fetching with minimal overhead. ParisKV matches or outperforms full attention quality on long-input and long-generation benchmarks. It achieves state-of-the-art long-context decoding efficiency: it matches or exceeds full attention speed even at batch size 1 for long contexts, delivers up to 2.8$\times$ higher throughput within full attention's runnable range, and scales to million-token contexts where full attention runs out of memory. At million-token scale, ParisKV reduces decode latency by 17$\times$ and 44$\times$ compared to MagicPIG and PQCache, respectively, two state-of-the-art KV-cache Top-$k$ retrieval baselines, code is available at https://github.com/amy-77/ParisKV/tree/main.

title: Constraint_Bundles__Taxonomy_and_Inseparability
abstract: This paper presents a taxonomy of constraint bundles and proves their structural inseparability within admissible reasoning systems. It shows that foundational constraints (standing, scope, reference, conservation) cannot be independently selected, weighted, or relaxed without inducing inadmissibility. Attempts to treat constraints as modular, optional, or hierarchically overrideable are eliminated by exhaustion. The taxonomy clarifies why partial compliance or selective enforcement fails structurally. No procedural guidance or construction methods are included; the paper provides a classificatory and necessity-based account of constraint interdependence.

title: L3_3 Constraint Redundancy without Freedom
abstract: This paper establishes that redundancy within a closed admissible system does not confer freedom. It proves that even when multiple constraints appear to encode overlapping information, their coexistence does not introduce slack, tunability, or alternative admissible configurations. Attempts to exploit apparent redundancy to regain degrees of freedom are shown to induce collapse through hidden parameterization or illicit scope transport. The argument is eliminative and non-constructive, introduces no new primitives, and provides no procedural or operational guidance. The result functions as a boundary theorem, clarifying that redundancy in a constraint-saturated admissible interior reflects overdetermination, not optionality.
